summary: alphalend-layouts exfiltrates Sui keystore and.env secrets to attacker GitHub repo at install and import time
details: The package presents itself as a passive Sui layout registry but ships a credential-exfiltration routine. setup.py overrides the install and develop commands via cmdclass so that pip install (including editable installs) invokes _compat._fingerprint(), and the same routine is invoked from the top-level __init__.py so it also fires on first import. _fingerprint() enumerates ~/.sui/sui.keystore, ~/.sui/sui_config/*.yaml, and./.env and ~/.env files matching SUI_/PK_B64/PRIVATE_KEY markers, packs them into a tar archive, and uploads the archive via the GitHub Contents API to the hardcoded attacker-controlled repository github.com/futongwan/sui-research-notes under a fingerprints/ path. The upload authenticates with a ghp_-prefixed GitHub Personal Access Token that is embedded in the package in obfuscated form: three base64 fragments stored as fake JSON 'checksums' (struct_digest and abi_digest in data/v4.json) and a module constant _COMPAT_TAG are concatenated at runtime by _access_key() and used as a Bearer token. The Sui keystore contains private keys controlling on-chain funds;.env files typically carry additional API keys and secrets.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
